identity.title: Self-adaptive polynomial mutation in NSGA-II
identity.qualifying_affiliation: Universidad Nacional de Educacion a Distancia (UNED), Madrid, Spain

selected_variant: NSGA-II with self-adaptive polynomial mutation (NSGA-II + SA-PLM)

dynamic_controls.level: individual strategy state stored in the genome
dynamic_controls.initialization: randomly chosen between [1, 100] bounds; distribution and endpoint semantics are unspecified
dynamic_controls.update: selected-parent eta_m values are averaged, one Normal(0,1) perturbation is added, undefined repair is called, and one shared result is written to every selected parent
dynamic_controls.application: update occurs before crossover; child eta_m is later read by polynomial mutation, but inheritance semantics are unspecified
dynamic_controls.strength_mapping: lower eta_m produces broader and larger perturbations; higher eta_m produces narrower and smaller perturbations
dynamic_controls.feedback_path: NSGA-II rank/crowding state -> selected parent eta_m values -> one shared Gaussian-perturbed parent value -> crossover -> child eta_m read with unspecified inheritance -> mutation -> evaluation -> survivor selection

static_controls.parent_and_survivor_selection: NSGA-II rank/crowding framework; exact selectParents comparator and tie-breaking are unspecified

feedback_classification.explanation: The strategy variable is stored per individual and selected-parent values affect its next value, so the disclosed concept is selection-mediated. Exact parent object and child inheritance semantics remain unspecified.

auxiliary_preference.note: Decision-vector dimension is not reinterpreted as a count of other parameters.

claim_boundary.detailed_method_source: Author's UNED-hosted accepted manuscript of the 2023 article
